transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just... having trouble talking, I guess. My words, they don't stay in a straight line anymore. 

Like, I'll start talking about an overnight shift at work... and then I just jump to soccer, or paint colors, or... patient charts. I don't really know why it happens. But I can see everyone getting lost when I do it. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself struggling to keep talking or does it just feel like your thoughts are jumping around?
I don't know... it's mostly just the jumping. Like I said. I don't really run out of words, they just... go to the wrong places. Like the paint or the charts. They just don't stay straight.
Do you have these problems with your thoughts jumping around all the time, or does it come and go?

It doesn't really go away. It's... it's been happening for a while now. Maybe a year? A year and a month, I think. Just... the words getting messed up, and the way I act. And... feeling like people are watching me. It's all been going on for about that long.
Do you really believe people are watching you, or is it just a feeling?

I... no, I know they are. It's not just a feeling. 

The supervisors at work... they changed my shifts. And I know they watch me on the unit cameras. They're trying to see if I'm... unsafe. People keep telling me it's just staffing shortages, but... I know what they're doing.
Have you been acting in ways that seem strange or unusual to other people?

I guess... maybe. I don't really ask them what they think. But... at work, yeah. 

Sometimes I'm in the hallway and I realize I'm just... rocking. Or if one of the patients is tapping on something, I catch myself copying them. Just tapping along. And... sometimes I just stop. Like I'll be putting my gloves on to do my rounds, and they're only half on, and I just stand there. Like I'm stuck. I know I'm supposed to be working, but... I just don't.
Can you tell me more about what happens when you just stop, like when you're putting on your gloves?

I don't really know what else to tell you. I just... stop. 

Like I said... the gloves are only half on, and I know I need to go do my rounds, but I just stand there. I'm just stuck. It's... it's just like when I catch myself rocking in the hall, or copying that tapping. I don't know why I do it. I just do.
Do you think your rocking, tapping, or stopping actions are related to anything in particular or do they seem to happen without a reason?
No... I don't think so. It just... happens. I don't have a reason for it.
When your words jump around, do they still make sense to you, or do you feel like you're not making sense even to yourself?

I... I don't really know if it makes sense to me. I just know I can't keep my words straight anymore. Like... I'll start talking about an overnight shift, and then somehow I'm talking about soccer, or paint colors, or... patient charts. I can tell people are getting lost. I just... can't keep it in a line.
When you say people are watching you, do you actually hear them talking about you or see them watching you?

I don't... hear them talking. Not really. But I know they are. 

I just... I know the supervisors watch me through the unit cameras. They changed my shifts. People keep telling me it's just staffing shortages, but... I know they're doing it to watch me. To see if I'm... unsafe. I just know it.
When you say you know the supervisors are watching you, is that something you think about all the time or just sometimes?

It's... pretty much all I think about. I know they're watching me. Like I said, they changed my shifts... and they watch the cameras. People keep saying it's just the staffing shortages, but... I know why they did it. They want to see if I'm unsafe. I just... I know it.
When you think about the supervisors watching you, does it feel like a clear and coherent idea to you or is it more of a vague feeling that you can't quite put into words?
It's... it's clear to me. I just... I know it. I don't really know how else to explain it.
When your words jump around, do you ever say things that don't make sense to you after you've said them?

Yeah... I guess. I just... I can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like... I'll start talking about an overnight shift... and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or... paint colors, or patient charts. I don't really know why. But I can see everyone getting lost when I do it. It just... happens.
When you're talking and your words jump around, do you feel like you're still trying to express one main idea, or does it feel like you're expressing multiple unrelated ideas at the same time?

I don't know... I guess I'm trying to make a point, but... it just doesn't come out right. Like I said, I'll be talking about a shift, and then... soccer, or paint, or charts. It's just... a mess. I don't know if it's one idea or... a bunch. It just doesn't stay straight.
When you're talking and your words are jumping around, do you feel like your emotions are also all over the place or hard to control?
Not really... I don't think so. I mostly just feel... I don't know. Just tired. It's just the words that do that.
When your words jump around, do you feel like it's something that's happening to you, or something you're doing intentionally?
I don't know... I'm definitely not doing it on purpose. It just... happens to me, I guess. That's all.
Do you find that when you're rocking, tapping, or stopping, your thoughts are also disjointed or hard to follow at the same time?

I'm not really sure what my thoughts are doing then. I just... I know at work, I've caught myself rocking in the hallway. Or... copying a patient when they're tapping. Sometimes I just get stuck. Like, I'll be standing there with my gloves half on, just stopped... even though I know I'm supposed to be doing my rounds. I don't really know what's in my head when it happens.
When you're talking and your words jump around, do you feel like you're still in control of what you're saying?
I don't really know. It's just... the words come out how they come out. I don't feel like I'm not in control, but I'm not really thinking about it either.
When your words jump around, do you think it's related to your feeling of being watched or is it something separate for you?

I guess they kind of happen together. When I get really down... like, at my worst... that's usually when I'm sure the supervisors are watching me through the cameras. And... my words just get so tangled. I can't really explain myself clearly if anyone asks me anything. So... yeah, it's connected.
Do you think the supervisors watching you is something that's really happening or something you're just worried about?

It's... it's really happening. I'm sure of it. They changed my shifts on purpose so they can watch me through the unit cameras. They want to see if I'm unsafe. People keep telling me it's just staffing shortages, but... I know it's not. I know what they're doing.
Do you think the way your words jump around is related to any stress or anxiety you might be feeling?
I don't know. Maybe. I'm just tired. I don't really think about it being stress... it's just how it is.
